title: Two-month sprint velocity reflection - personal KPI notebook
content:
Purpose
- Capture what I actually shipped and how that maps to the personal KPIs I set at the start of the quarter.
- Make explicit which habit/rituals influenced velocity and which blockers repeated.
- Propose 3 concrete experiments to improve focus and output for the next two-month cycle.

Context
- Two-month focus window (Jan 5 - Mar 5) I set for: 1) stabilizing the LLM cache eviction heuristic (perf + reliability), 2) finishing the ‘smart-batching’ prototype POC, 3) deep-dive on cost-per-token analysis for mid-tail workloads.
- Personal KPIs at start:
  * KPI-A: Deliver 2 production-grade PRs that reduce 95th P90 latency variance by >=5% on test harness.
  * KPI-B: Run 6 focused experiments (one / week on average) across batching/config to reduce cost-per-token by 8%.
  * KPI-C: Maintain weekly uninterrupted focus blocks of 3x90mins to support deep work.

Summary of outcomes
- PRs merged: 1 full PR to prod for cache heuristic (merged Feb 14), 1 prototype merged to staging for smart-batching (merged Mar 2 but not rolled out). Result: KPI-A partially met (1/2 merged, latency variance improvement measured at 3.6% on p95 in canary workloads).
- Experiments completed: 4 full experiments (detailed below), 2 aborted/paused due to infra constraints (GPU queue delays, dataset mismatch). Net estimated cost improvement across completed experiments ~4.5%. KPI-B not met.
- Focus blocks: Average per week = 2.1 blocks (goal 3). Several weeks with zero due to on-call rotation and PR review blitz. KPI-C not met.

Detailed log (week-by-week highlights)
- Week 1 (Jan 5-11): Kickoffs, defined acceptance criteria for caching PR. Set up synthetic test harness (latency runners).
- Week 2 (Jan 12-18): Initial model of eviction weights; found regressions when sequence length > 1k. Paused for instrumentation.
- Week 3 (Jan 19-25): Instrumentation landed; reproduced variance flaps. Began experiment A (decoupled cold-start thresholds).
- Week 4 (Jan 26-Feb 1): Experiment A showed small gains under synthetic load. Started Experiment B (KV prefetching policy).
- Week 5 (Feb 2-8): Finalized cache heuristic PR; code review heavy. Lost 2 planned focus blocks because of cross-team alignment meetings.
- Week 6 (Feb 9-15): Cache PR merged Feb 14. Canary results: p95 latency variance down 3.6%, cost neutral. Began drafting smart-batching POC.
- Week 7 (Feb 16-22): Smart-batching POC implemented; infra GPU queue issues hit Feb 20-21, causing aborted experiments.
- Week 8 (Feb 23-Mar 1): Re-ran experiments with smaller batch sizes; produced prototype (merged to staging Mar 2). Started cost-per-token analysis deep-dive.

Experiment inventory (short notes)
- Experiment A: Cold-start threshold tuning (Jan 19-25)
  * Hypothesis: Raising cold threshold from 8->12 will reduce cache churn on long-seq sessions.
  * Outcome: Reduced eviction churn under synthetic long sessions, negligible effect on normal traffic.
  * Next: Combine with weighted TTL to avoid regressions.
- Experiment B: KV prefetching policy (Jan 26-Feb 1)
  * Hypothesis: Proactively fetching likely KV pages reduces p95 during bursts.
  * Outcome: Improved p95 under burst sims but increased average token cost by ~2%. Decided to hold until batching POC available.
- Experiment C: Smart-batching priority rule (Feb 17-23)
  * Hypothesis: Priority grouping by seq-length reduces GPU context-switch overhead.
  * Outcome: Prototype shows 6% throughput gain in staging, but infra instability prevents production rollout.
- Experiment D: Token-level cache compression (Feb 24-Mar 1)
  * Hypothesis: Lightweight compression reduces memory pressure and prevents eviction.
  * Outcome: Promising in local sim; high CPU overhead in current nodes. Need to revisit with hardware team.

Metrics snapshot (notes, not authoritative numbers)
- Merge rate: 2 PRs merged, 1 in staging.
- Focus blocks: target 3/week, actual ~2.1/week.
- Experiments started: 6, completed 4.
- Measured p95 variance improvement (canary): ~3.6% from cache PR.
- Estimated cost delta from experiments: -4.5% (partial) vs target -8%.

Root causes for missed targets
- Fragmented calendar: recurring meetings and high-context switching. I underestimated effort for cross-team alignment (instrumentation + infra changes).
- Infra blockers: GPU queue instability and dataset mismatches delayed two experiments and forced smaller-scale tests that had lower sensitivity.
- Over-optimistic experiment scope: some experiments assumed infra changes that required SRE involvement and additional approvals.

Personal reflexive notes (less polished)
- My week zero and week six were high-activation weeks where I could sustain focus; the other weeks had either meetings or review pressure. Pattern: PR merge sprint consumes attention for 7-10 days, then a drop-off.
- I default to reactive mode when multiple reviews land. Need guardrails: scheduled review windows, and pair-reviewing for large PRs.
- The habit I neglected: daily 15-minute morning planning. When I skip it I lose the thread on experiment steps.

Action items & experiments for next two-month window (Mar 15 - May 15)
1) Structural experiments (priority):
   - Experiment X: Combine bucketed batching with KV prefetching; small-scale rollout to dedicated infra (requires infra sign-off). Success metric: +4% throughput at <=1% cost increase.
   - Experiment Y: Lightweight token compression on head nodes only (A/B) to test CPU tradeoff. Success metric: reduces memory churn and reduces cold-start evictions by 8%.
2) Operational improvements:
   - Block calendar: 3x90min focus blocks on Tues/Thu mornings; set Slack status and automated 'reviews only' windows.
   - Weekly timeboxed review: set Monday 45m to plan the week and log experiment hypotheses.
3) Collaboration requests:
   - Ask infra (SRE) for a 2-day dedicated runway to run GPU-heavy batch experiments (raise JIRA INF-987).
   - Pair with Kai for two review windows on major PRs; adopt a "review buddy" rule for any >500-line changes.

Metrics & acceptance criteria for next window (define before starting each experiment)
- Throughput: measure tokens/sec at 95th percentile across staging harness. Target +3–5% for priority experiments.
- Cost: cost-per-token measured across representative mid-tail dataset. Target <= +1% for any throughput-focused change, net improvement target -7% across combined efforts.
- Stability: no increase in error rate >0.2% and no SLO violations in the 99th percentile latency.

Notes to self (short checklist)
- [ ] Draft the Experiment X RFC and link to JIRA (due Mar 12).
- [ ] Book 2-day infra runway (email SRE and escalate if not acknowledged in 48h).
- [ ] Re-instate morning planning ritual for 4 consecutive weeks and log adherence.
- [ ] Pair with Kai for the next big review.

Final reflections (high level)
- Progress felt real (one merged PR with measurable impact), but compound gains require more reliable infra and better calendar hygiene.
- The two-month cadence is a good fit for experiments that need multiple iteration loops; still need to plan for the PR-sprint troughs.
- Priority for the next window: reduce blockers (infra + approvals) and enforce personal rituals that preserve deep work.

Appendix: quick links + references
- Linked confluence draft for caching spec: CONFLUENCE-1234
- JIRA tasks: JIRA-INF-987 (infra runway), JIRA-ENG-3012 (batching POC)
- Staging benchmark results: github.com/redwood/benchmarks/runs/2402 (internal)

-- end of note --
